from manim import *
import numpy as np

class TeachingScene(Scene):
    def setup_layout(self, title_text, lecture_lines):
        # BASE
        self.camera.background_color = "#000000"
        self.title = Text(title_text, font_size=28, color=WHITE).to_edge(UP)
        self.add(self.title)

        # Left-side lecture content (bullets with "-")
        lecture_texts = [Text(line, font_size=22, color=WHITE) for line in lecture_lines]
        self.lecture = VGroup(*lecture_texts).arrange(DOWN, aligned_edge=LEFT).scale(0.8)
        self.lecture.to_edge(LEFT, buff=0.2)
        self.add(self.lecture)

        # Define fine-grained animation grid (4x4 grid on right side)
        self.grid = {}
        rows = ["A", "B", "C", "D", "E", "F"]  # Top to bottom
        cols = ["1", "2", "3", "4", "5", "6"]  # Left to right

        for i, row in enumerate(rows):
            for j, col in enumerate(cols):
                x = 0.5 + j * 1
                y = 2.2 - i * 1
                self.grid[f"{row}{col}"] = np.array([x, y, 0])

    def place_at_grid(self, mobject, grid_pos, scale_factor=1.0):
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(self.grid[grid_pos])
        return mobject

    def place_in_area(self, mobject, top_left, bottom_right, scale_factor=1.0):
        tl_pos = self.grid[top_left]
        br_pos = self.grid[bottom_right]
        
        # Calculate center of the area
        center_x = (tl_pos[0] + br_pos[0]) / 2
        center_y = (tl_pos[1] + br_pos[1]) / 2
        center = np.array([center_x, center_y, 0])
        
        mobject.scale(scale_factor)
        mobject.move_to(center)
        return mobject

        self.wait(2)

    def construct(self):

            "Slope fields visualize possible paths.",
            "Solutions follow the field's directions."

        axes = Axes(x_range=[0, 3], y_range=[0, 3], axis_config={"include_tip": False})

        ))
        
        self.place_in_area(axes, 'D2', 'F5', scale_factor=0.5)

        self.play(Create(axes), Create(field))
        self.play(self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))

class Section3Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        lecture_lines = [
            "Solving ODEs means reversing derivatives.",
            "We integrate the field's slope.",
            "This reveals the function's path."
        ]
        self.setup_layout("The Core Mechanics: Solving via Integration", lecture_lines)
        
        # Elements
        derivative_obj = MathTex(r"\frac{dy}{dt}", color=WHITE)
        integral_sign = MathTex(r"\int dt", color="#00FFFF")
        function_path = MathTex(r"y(t) = t^2 + C", color=WHITE)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        self.place_at_grid(derivative_obj, 'B3', scale_factor=2.0)
        self.play(Write(derivative_obj))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(GREY), self.lecture[1].animate.set_color("#00FFFF"))
        self.place_at_grid(integral_sign, 'D3', scale_factor=2.0)
        self.play(Write(integral_sign))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(GREY), self.lecture[2].animate.set_color(WHITE))
        self.place_at_grid(function_path, 'D5', scale_factor=1.5)
        self.play(ReplacementTransform(derivative_obj.copy(), function_path), FadeIn(function_path))
        self.wait(2)

class Section4Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Initial Conditions: Pinning Down the Solution", 
                          ["Families of curves share formulas.", 
                           "Constants leave solutions flexible.", 
                           "Initial points fix the solution."])
        
        # Axes
        axes = Axes(x_range=[0, 5], y_range=[0, 5], axis_config={"include_tip": True}).scale(0.6)
        self.place_at_grid(axes, "C3")

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Show family of curves
        curves = VGroup()
        for c in [0.5, 1.0, 1.5, 2.0]:
            curve = axes.plot(lambda t: c * np.exp(0.3 * t), color=BLUE)
            curve.set_opacity(0.5)
            curves.add(curve)
        
        self.play(Create(curves), self.lecture[0].animate.set_color(BLUE))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Highlight flexibility
        self.play(self.lecture[1].animate.set_color(YELLOW))
        self.play(Indicate(curves))
        self.wait(1)

        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Add initial point
        point = Dot(axes.c2p(2, 2), color="#FF9900")
        self.place_at_grid(point, "C3") # Relative to axes
        
        target_curve = axes.plot(lambda t: 1.09 * np.exp(0.3 * t), color=WHITE)
        
        self.play(FadeIn(point), self.lecture[2].animate.set_color("#FF9900"))
        self.play(Transform(curves, target_curve))
        self.wait(2)

class Section5Scene(TeachingScene):
    def construct(self):
        self.setup_layout("Real-World Synthesis & Wrap-up", ["ODEs model our changing world.", "They turn physics into predictions.", "Now you can model dynamics."])
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 1 ===
        # Display title 'Real-World Synthesis' in #FFFFFF.
        self.lecture[0].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 2 ===
        # Show oscillating spring model in #00FF00.
        self.lecture[1].set_color("#00FF00")
        
        # Simple Spring representation
        spring = VGroup()
        for i in range(10):
            spring.add(Line(ORIGIN, RIGHT * 0.2 + UP * 0.2 if i % 2 == 0 else RIGHT * 0.2 + DOWN * 0.2))
        spring.arrange(RIGHT, buff=0)
        mass = Square(side_length=0.5, color=GREEN, fill_opacity=0.5)
        spring_system = VGroup(spring, mass).arrange(RIGHT, buff=0.1)
        
        self.place_at_grid(spring_system, 'B3', scale_factor=1.2)
        self.play(Create(spring_system), run_time=2)
        self.play(spring_system.animate.shift(LEFT * 0.5), spring_system.animate.shift(RIGHT * 0.5), run_time=1.5, rate_func=there_and_back)
        
        # === Animation for Lecture Line 3 ===
        # Fade to final summary text in #FFFFFF.
        self.lecture[2].set_color("#FFFFFF")
        self.play(FadeIn(self.lecture[2]), run_time=1)
        self.wait(2)

sections.title: The Hook: Dynamics in Motion
sections.content: Introduce the concept of a rate of change using a visual of a cheetah chasing prey. Emphasize that we often know how fast something is changing (velocity/acceleration) but need to find the position function over time.
sections.example: A cheetah's velocity is proportional to its distance from the prey; how do we describe its position at any time t?

sections.title: Defining the ODE: The Mathematical Bridge
sections.content: Define an ODE as an equation involving a function and its derivatives. Use a graphical split-screen: the left side shows a slope field (arrows representing local derivatives), and the right side shows a smooth curve (the solution) threading through the field.
sections.example: dy/dt = ky (The growth of a bacterial colony where the rate of growth is proportional to the current population size).

sections.title: The Core Mechanics: Solving via Integration
sections.content: Explain that solving an ODE is essentially 'reversing' the derivative. Visually demonstrate the process by 'integrating' the slope field arrows to reconstruct the function path.
sections.example: Given dy/dt = 2t, we integrate both sides to find y(t) = t² + C, where 'C' represents the family of all possible starting positions.

sections.title: Initial Conditions: Pinning Down the Solution
sections.content: Explain the role of the constant 'C'. Use a visual 'slider' that moves the solution curve up and down; show that a single point (Initial Condition) is required to select the specific curve from the family of solutions.
sections.example: If the bacterial colony starts with 10 cells at t=0, C=10, giving us the unique solution y(t) = 10e^(kt).

sections.title: Real-World Synthesis & Wrap-up
sections.content: Summarize that ODEs are the language of change. Revisit the cheetah example: by knowing the physics (derivative), we solve the equation (integral) to predict exactly where the cheetah will be at any time.
sections.example: Applying ODEs to a smartphone battery drain: dV/dt = -k(V) helps us predict exactly when the device will turn off.
